newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BellSouth NZ takes Telecom to court.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth NZ takes Telecom to court.

text.p: BellSouth New Zealand said on Thursday it had lodged proceedings in the Auckland High Court against Telecom Corp of NZ for what it alleged was price and service bundling by Telecom.
BellSouth also alleged Telecom had misused confidential commercial information.
"BellSouth's legal action highlights what it believes are anti-competitive discounting practices from Telecom in recent years," BellSouth said in a statement.
"Those practices include offering discounts in markets where Telecom has a monopoly, in return for exclusive relationships in markets where Telecom has competition," it said.
Those practices were features of Telecom's "Premier" and "Telecom Connect" plans offered to thousands of businesses.
BellSouth's General Manager, Legal, Kiran Chhaganlal, said applying discounts across both monopoly and contestable services by a dominant company could contravene the Commerce Act.

Chhaganlal pointed to the Commerce Commission's successful prosecution of Port Nelson Ltd (PNL) over the company's use of its dominant position to prevent Tasman Bay Marine Pilots Ltd competing with it.
Bundling had been of deep concern to the industry for some time and was one factor that had stifled competition, BellSouth said.

"The Commerce Commission has taken insufficient heed of these problems, despite concern from many quarters. We therefore have no choice but to pursue the matter through the High Court," Chhaganlal said.
Many businesses had been tied into contracts with Telecom, based on bundled discounts, which exclude them from lower cost service options, BellSouth said.
BellSouth also alleged that Telecom was misusing confidential customer information that BellSouth must provide Telecom in order for calls to pass between the two networks.
Telecom Media Communications Manager Clive Litt said in separate statement that the action was an attempt to "hobble" Telecom's ability to compete.
"They (the allegations) have no substance and we welcome the opportunity to challenge them before an independent, impartial body," he said. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
